cohort: The study included 200 consecutive patients presenting to the labour room for delivery at 7 Air Force Hospital, Kanpur.
finding: Despite a high prevalence of vitamin D insufficiency/deficiency (79%) among pregnant women, no statistically significant association was established with adverse pregnancy outcomes.
mod_finding: Primary cesarean sections showed no significant correlation with vitamin D status.
cross-section timing: Vitamin D levels were measured at the time of delivery between August and December 2023.
